model.rationale: An incumbent in a D+15 seat holding a hundred-to-one fundraising edge over her challenger faces little realistic threat, and market pricing near 98% reinforces the district fundamentals. With no polls to contradict them, everything points to a comfortable Scanlon win.

overview:
PA-05 is a strongly Democratic district in the Philadelphia suburbs, rated D+15, and Mary Gay Scanlon returns as the incumbent after renomination. No public general-election polls track the race and national expert raters have not listed it, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, campaign finance, and market pricing. Scanlon has raised roughly $990,000 and holds about $449,000 on hand, while Republican Nicholas Manganaro has raised about $9,300 with no outside spending on either side.

Prediction markets give the Democratic side about a 98 percent chance of holding the seat. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money advantage points to a comfortable Scanlon win, with the main uncertainty coming from how the national environment moves suburban voters rather than from the challenger's campaign.
